title: Full State-Size DFA Security for DEFAULT
summary: DEFAULT’s methodology can achieve almost-full DFA security, while attainability of full state-size security within the methodology remains open.

formal_statement.body: For DEFAULT's DFA-security methodology, determine whether full state-size DFA security is attainable. The methodology can achieve almost-full DFA security, but current evidence only suggests that full state-size security may be impossible. Settle the question by either attaining full state-size DFA security within the methodology or establishing that the methodology cannot attain it.

scope.domain: Differential fault analysis security of the DEFAULT block-cipher methodology.
parameters: state size — defines the target level for full state-size DFA security
number of S-box linear structures — controls the methodology's DFA search complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the methodology can attain full state-size DFA security, or prove that it cannot.

citations.label: DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack

progress.summary: The source presents almost-full DFA security as technically achievable but says full state-size security does not seem possible under the methodology, leaving a construction-or-impossibility challenge.
citation_labels: Anubhab Baksi et al., DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack
